function.name: calc_heat_capacity
function.description: Calculate the heat capacity at constant pressure of air using its temperature and volume. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

temp.description: The temperature of the gas in Kelvin.

volume.description: The volume of the gas in m^3.

gas.description: Type of gas, with air as default.

message.reasoning:
The user wants calculation of heat capacity at constant pressure (Cp) for air given T=298 K, V=10 m³. They didn't specify if they want per mole? Usually Cp depends only on composition not volume; but maybe use ideal gas law PV=nRT -> n=P*V/(R*T). But we don't have P. For standard conditions, assume atmospheric pressure ~101325 Pa. Then compute n. R=8.314 J/mol·K. So n = P*V / (R*T). Compute: P*V = 101325 * 10 = 1,013,250 J/K? Wait units: Pa*m³ = N/m² * m³ = Nm = Joule. Actually PV has unit J. Dividing by RT gives mol count.

Compute n: 1,013,250 / (8.314*298)=1,013,250/2477.772 ≈408.9 mol. Air's Cp≈29.1 J/mol*K (for diatomic gases). Multiply: C_p_total = n*C_p_mol = 408.9*29.1 ≈11900 J/K. Alternatively could give specific heat capacity per mass etc. Provide explanation.

We need to call function calc_heat_capacity? That expects temp, volume, gas optional. It will likely calculate something internally. We can provide arguments: temp=298, volume=10, gas="air". Let's do it.
